question.prompt: Let \(S\) be the set of all positive integer divisors of \(100{,}000.\) How many numbers are the product of two distinct elements of \(S?\)

solutions.title: Count possible prime exponents
solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that prime exponents identify each possible product uniquely. Since
\[
100{,}000=2^5 5^5,
\]
every divisor in \(S\) has the form \(2^i5^j\), where \(0\le i,j\le5\). A product of two such divisors therefore has the form \(2^a5^b\), with \(0\le a,b\le10\). There are \(11\cdot11=121\) candidate exponent pairs.

Four pairs are impossible when the factors must be distinct:
\[
(0,0),\quad(0,10),\quad(10,0),\quad(10,10).
\]
Indeed, an exponent sum of \(0\) forces both corresponding exponents to be \(0\), and a sum of \(10\) forces both to be \(5\). At each of these four corners, the two factors must therefore be equal.

To prove that every remaining pair works, use these factorizations:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{Range}&\text{First factor}&\text{Second factor}\\ \hline
0\le a\le5,\ 0\le b\le5&1&2^a5^b\\
6\le a\le10,\ 0\le b\le5&2^5&2^{a-5}5^b\\
0\le a\le5,\ 6\le b\le10&5^5&2^a5^{b-5}\\
6\le a\le10,\ 6\le b\le10&2^55^5&2^{a-5}5^{b-5}
\end{array}
\]
Both factors in each row belong to \(S\), and they are equal only at the excluded corner in that row. The four ranges cover all exponent pairs without overlap. Also, unique prime factorization ensures that different pairs give different products.

Thus the number of products is
\[
121-4=\boxed{117},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
